sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 26.0% a year from $4.32 billion in FY2016 to $34.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F231].
The path was a step change, not a straight line: revenue rose 68.3% in FY2021 and 43.6% in FY2022, then fell 3.9% in FY2023 before recovering 13.7% and 34.3% [D258][D314][D370][D426][D483].
The FY2022 jump included the Xilinx acquisition, which added Embedded revenue of $4.55 billion against $246 million a year earlier [S110][S109][P41].
The FY2023 decline came from a 25% drop in Client revenue on weak PC demand and inventory correction, partly offset by Embedded [P35].
Data Center revenue reached $16.6 billion in FY2025, 48.0% of total revenue, and contributed 15.7pp of the 34.3% growth [S98][D692][D694][D483].
The filing attributes that growth to strong demand for 5th generation AMD EPYC processors and AMD Instinct MI350 Series GPUs [P15].
Client and Gaming added 19.0pp, with Client revenue of $10.6 billion up 51% on a 31% rise in processor units and a 15% rise in average selling price [D701][S124][P10].
Operating income grew 94.4% against 34.3% revenue growth, an incremental operating margin of 20.3% [D484][D483][D511].
Diluted EPS rose 165.0% against 164.2% net income growth, as the diluted share count was flat at -0.1% [D487][D485][D506].
Gross margin of 49.5% is the window high, against a 44.7% median [F40][D800][D801].
Operating margin of 10.7% sits above the 7.2% window median but far below the 22.2% FY2021 high [F60][D795][D794].
In FY2025 cost of revenue added only 0.2pp to operating margin, while SG&A subtracted 1.2pp and R&D added 1.7pp [D513][D515][D514].
Gross margin improved on product mix, partly offset by about $440 million of MI308 inventory and related charges tied to U.S. export controls [P14].
Net margin of 12.5% exceeded operating margin by 1.9pp, helped by $577 million of other income from unrealized investment gains and a $103 million tax benefit [F80][F60][D843][P5][P4].
Operating cash flow was $7.71 billion and free cash flow $6.74 billion in FY2025, a 19.4% free-cash-flow margin [F110][F130][D467].
Free cash flow was 1.55x net income against a 1.17x window median [D471][D810].
Operating cash flow was reduced by a $2.2 billion inventory build to support the Data Center ramp [P3].
Capex of $974 million was 2.8% of revenue and 1.87x D&A, the highest ratio in the window [F120][D466][D472].
Cash and investments of $10.6 billion against $4.10 billion of debt left net cash of $6.46 billion, 18.6% of revenue [D474][D475][D476][D477].
That net cash position ranks at the 100th percentile of five semis peers, whose median is -17.3% of revenue [D844][D845].
Debt rose 138% to $4.10 billion, including $1.5 billion of notes issued in March 2025 [D508][D475][P6].
Buybacks of $1.32 billion were 19.5% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count was flat [X150][D479][D506].
Revenue fell 3.9% in FY2023, the only decline in the window, driven by Client and Gaming weakness [D370][P35].
Total debt rose 138% in FY2025 to $4.10 billion, though net cash still rose to $6.46 billion [D508][D475][D476].
The effective tax rate moved -21.3pp to -2.5% on an $853 million uncertain-tax-position release, so the FY2025 net margin is not a clean run rate [D469][D412][P4].
Days inventory outstanding rose to 165 days from 160, extending a climb from 106 days in FY2022 [D481][D424][D312].
Data Center operating margin fell to 21.7% from 27.7%; a further move below the FY2023 level of 19.5% would confirm margin pressure [D769][D768][D767].
Operating margin of 10.7% is below the 22.2% window high; a recovery above the 7.2% median would confirm the FY2025 trend, reported in the FY2026 10-K [F60][D794][D795].
Days inventory outstanding of 165 days against 160 in FY2024; a move back toward the 106-day FY2022 level would ease the working-capital drag [D481][D424][D312].
